newsitem.title: FRANCE: DHL Strasbourg hub project in doubt.
newsitem.headline: DHL Strasbourg hub project in doubt.

text.p: DHL Worldwide Express said it had not given up hope of going ahead with a project to set up a regional air cargo hub at Strasbourg-Entzheim Airport, despite a recent statement by the local council.

The council had previously been in favour of the project but in the light of local protests over aircraft noise during night-time periods it commissioned an impact study to establish the environmental and economic impacts of DHL's project, market sources said.

In the statement, which followed the preliminary conclusions of the impact study, the council said: "Given the current state of technology to limit aircraft noise emissions, we consider intensive night-time flying at Strasbourg airport to be inadvisable."
The statement added that it was crucial that regulations be put in place governing night-time operations at the airport.
"Clearly we are disappointed by the council's remarks but we don't want to say too much at this stage," said Steven Lewis, DHL Aviation's business development manager, told Reuters from Brussels.
He said DHL would be seeking detailed clarification from the council on several points in the statement.

"There is talk of the airport's environmental committee drawing up a proposals document on the conditions for DHL's location at Strasbourg and hopefully, we'd have the opportunity of presenting our case once again," he said.
The proposals document would be submitted to the French Secretary of State for Transport and the French civil aviation authority, the DGAC, with whom a final decision on the project would rest.
Some political leaders in the Strasbourg area and civic and environmental protection groups are opposed to the project arguing that flights would disrupt the local people's sleep.
By contrast, the Strasbourg Chamber of Commerce, which runs the airport, today published a full-page advertisement in the French national press in favour DHL's project.
It said it had received letters from 2,000 businesses in the region supporting the express operator's project.
DHL had planned to debut at Strasbourg airport with one or two night flights using Convair and Electra aircraft, during the final quarter of 1996 - rising to seven flights nightly in 1997.
The flights would link Strasbourg with its European hub at Brussels and the express company's regional hubs.

In an initial three to four year phase of operation, DHL would invest US$5 million at the site, creating 350 jobs. And then it plans to move into a US$50 million purpose-built facility, around the turn of the century as traffic volumes increase, the spokesman added.

"Strasbourg remains our firm choice and at this point in time we are not looking at an alternative site. However, on the other hand, we are not prepared to wait indefinitely for a decision," Lewis added."
